facts.text: A dozer pushes earth and rock with a wide front blade, while a grader levels and shapes road surfaces with a long angled blade under its body.
facts.quote: A dozer pushes earth and rock with a wide blade at the front, and a grader levels and shapes road surfaces with a long angled blade under its body.

facts.text: The booklet quotes a Caterpillar D11 dozer at about 107 t.
facts.quote: the booklet quotes a Caterpillar D11 at about 107 t [Chapter 8]

facts.text: Dozers and graders move slowly, work close to other machines and reverse often.
facts.quote: Both move slowly, work close to other machines and reverse often.

facts.text: At a tip head, a dozer pushes material while loaded trucks drive up, turn and back in, placing machines in shared tight spaces.
facts.quote: They appear in the record where machines share tight spaces. At a tip head a dozer pushes material while loaded trucks drive up, turn and back in.

facts.text: New Zealand's regulator described a D10 dozer reversing into the wheel of a loaded 777 truck at a tip head.
facts.quote: New Zealand's regulator described a D10 dozer reversing into the wheel of a loaded 777 truck at a tip head

facts.text: New Zealand's regulator described a reversing truck clipping a dozer at night.
facts.quote: New Zealand's regulator described a D10 dozer reversing into the wheel of a loaded 777 truck at a tip head, and a reversing truck clipping a dozer at night [Chapter 4].

facts.text: In New South Wales, a light vehicle entering a tip-head area was struck by a reversing dozer, killing the light-vehicle driver.
facts.quote: In New South Wales a light vehicle entering a tip-head area was struck by a reversing dozer, and the driver died [Chapter 4].

facts.text: A grader and a haul truck collided, causing major damage to both machines.
facts.quote: A grader and a haul truck collided with "major damage to both machines" [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Tracked machines brake differently from wheeled machines because tracks retain more grip in soft soil than tires.
facts.quote: Tracked machines also brake differently: tracks keep more grip in soft soil than tires

facts.text: Slow crawler machines have their own brake standard, ISO 10265.
facts.quote: slow crawlers have their own brake standard, ISO 10265 [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Dozers and graders are typical of heavy-machine-to-heavy-machine contacts, which the booklet ranks as the most frequently reported collision type, although these contacts usually cause property damage.
facts.quote: Dozers and graders are typical of heavy-machine-to-heavy-machine contacts, which the booklet ranks as the most frequently reported collision type even though it is usually property damage [Chapter 4].

facts.text: A braking system for dozers and graders must handle a tracked machine's stopping behavior.
facts.quote: A braking system must handle a tracked machine's stopping behavior

facts.text: A braking system for dozers and graders must not treat every nearby truck at a tip head as an emergency.
